title: Earthquake: prepare ahead
body: Identify safe spots in each room, such as under a sturdy table, and know the exits. Secure heavy furniture and shelves to walls. Keep a go-bag with water, food, flashlight, radio, first aid kit, medicines, and copies of important documents. Agree on a family meeting place.
source: General preparedness guidance (verify against PHIVOLCS / NDRRMC materials)

title: Earthquake: during shaking
body: DROP to your hands and knees, take COVER under a sturdy table or against an interior wall while protecting your head and neck, and HOLD ON until the shaking stops. Stay away from windows and heavy objects that can fall. If outdoors, move away from buildings, posts, and power lines. If driving, stop in a clear area and stay inside.
source: General preparedness guidance (verify against PHIVOLCS / NDRRMC materials)

title: Earthquake: after shaking stops
body: Expect aftershocks and be ready to drop, cover, and hold on again. Check yourself and others for injuries. Leave damaged buildings carefully and use stairs, not elevators. If you smell gas, open windows and leave, and do not use lighters or switches. Listen to official channels for updates.
source: General preparedness guidance (verify against PHIVOLCS / NDRRMC materials)

title: Typhoon: prepare ahead
body: Follow PAGASA bulletins and local government advisories. Secure loose objects outside and check your roof and windows. Charge phones and power banks. Prepare a go-bag with water, food, medicines, flashlight, and documents in waterproof bags. Know your nearest evacuation center and the route to it.
source: General preparedness guidance (verify against PAGASA / NDRRMC materials)

title: Typhoon: during the storm
body: Stay indoors away from windows and glass doors. Keep your phone charged and a radio tuned to official updates. Avoid going outside during strong winds, and do not cross flooded roads or rivers. Turn off the main power switch if water enters the house.
source: General preparedness guidance (verify against PAGASA / NDRRMC materials)

title: Flood: staying safe
body: Move to higher ground if water is rising. Do not walk or drive through floodwater, because even shallow moving water can be dangerous. Stay away from fallen power lines and turn off electricity if it is safe to do so. Keep important documents and medicines in a waterproof bag.
source: General preparedness guidance (verify against NDRRMC / Red Cross materials)

title: Flood: after the water recedes
body: Return home only when local authorities say it is safe. Floodwater may be contaminated, so avoid contact and wash hands often. Have electrical systems and gas checked before use. Throw away food that touched floodwater and drink only safe water.
source: General preparedness guidance (verify against NDRRMC / Red Cross materials)

title: Fire: if a fire starts
body: Alert everyone and get out immediately. Crawl low under smoke. Check doors with the back of your hand before opening, and do not open a hot door. Once outside, stay out and call the fire hotline or 911. Do not go back inside for belongings.
source: General preparedness guidance (verify against BFP materials)

title: Landslide: warning signs and action
body: Warning signs include cracks in the ground or walls, tilting trees or posts, and unusual sounds or muddy water in streams after heavy rain. If you notice them, move away from the slope immediately and tell your barangay officials. Never cross a landslide area.
source: General preparedness guidance (verify against MGB / NDRRMC materials)

title: Volcanic ash: protecting yourself
body: Stay indoors and close windows and doors. Wear a mask or damp cloth over your nose and mouth, and protect your eyes. Keep pets and water sources covered. Follow PHIVOLCS alert levels and local government instructions.
source: General preparedness guidance (verify against PHIVOLCS materials)
